we_do_better: Techniques vs. tools distinction — we separate reusable methods (Skills) from products (Tools), which no competitor does; uniquely valuable for practitioners
Source transparency — video quality badges, low-quality flags, and endorsement counts let users judge credibility at a glance; competitors show no provenance
MCP/connector tracking — dedicated Connectors tab covering 48 MCP servers is a niche no competitor addresses
Live RSS news feed merged with video-sourced news, covering 50+ authoritative AI sources alongside the playlist
Self-improvement system and open audit trail (merge log, deleted skills, suggestion queue) — competitors are static catalogs
Knowledge depth — 209 skills and 312 tools with quality scoring, vs competitors' unscored flat lists
Fully free, open-source, no ads, no paywall
they_do_better: Visual thumbnails and tool logos — Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, and Toolify show product images; our wall of text cards is slower to scan
Item-count badges per category — Future Tools and TAAFT display count per filter tab so users know scope before clicking
Simultaneous multi-axis filtering — Toolify lets users filter by category + pricing + rating at once; we only support single-axis filter
Hero section and featured/trending slots — all four competitors surface a 'start here' section; we drop visitors into an unlabelled card list
Sort controls — competitors offer newest / top-rated / most-popular sort; our Skills and Tools tabs sort only by quality score with no user control
User-generated signals — Product Hunt shows upvotes; TAAFT shows user saves; our popularity is editorial (video endorsement counts), not crowd-sourced
borrow_next: Add item-count badges to tab nav buttons (e.g. 'Skills (209)', 'Tools (312)') — one line of JS per tab from loaded JSON arrays, not stale status.json; ~10 lines total
Add a sort toggle (Quality | Mentions | Newest) to the Skills and Tools tabs — ~20 lines of JS, closes the biggest gap vs Toolify/Future Tools for power users
Add a color-coded left-border to skill/tool cards by score band (green ≥8, amber 6–7, grey <6) — one CSS rule per band, gives instant visual hierarchy with no images needed

findings.detail: TODAY = datetime(2026, 6, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc) is hardcoded at module level. compute_age_months() uses this frozen date, so all recency penalties after June 3 2026 are wrong — videos now appear ~10 days older than they are and the drift grows every day. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace with datetime.now(timezone.utc) computed inside compute_age_months at call time, not at module level.

findings.detail: load_json and save_json open files without encoding='utf-8'. Hebrew transcripts and Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 locale runners. src/fetch.py uses encoding='utf-8' consistently; analyze_batch.py does not. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to every open() call in load_json (L153) and save_json (L161). Also fix the remaining bare open() calls at lines 402, 725-726, 747-748.

findings.detail: process_video.py has its own duplicated load_json/save_json with the same missing encoding='utf-8' as analyze_batch.py. _write_skill_md() also opens SKILL.md output with bare open(). All three fail on Hebrew-sourced or Unicode-named content. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to load_json, save_json, and _write_skill_md in process_video.py. Consolidate load_json/save_json into a shared src/utils.py to prevent divergence recurring.

findings.detail: no_transcript=76, new_found=76 — 100% transcript fallback rate this run (all 76 new videos fell back to description or title). The broad except-all in fetch_transcript() silently swallows failures. This is the root cause of the 72% empty news summary crisis. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING before falling back. Add a health flag: if no_transcript / new_found > 0.5, set status['transcript_health'] = 'degraded' and show an amber dashboard banner. Verify youtube-transcript-api version compatibility.

findings.detail: describe_tool() returns a hardcoded category-keyed string regardless of video content. 33 of 312 tools (10.6%) now have template descriptions — down from 31.4% proportionally because the library grew 2.5×, but the absolute count of fakes barely moved and the root cause is unfixed. Each analyze_batch.py run adds more fakes.
findings.suggestion: Replace describe_tool() with extraction from the transcript: use the 1–2 sentences in the video that most concisely describe what the tool does. If no sentence qualifies, set description to null and show 'Description not yet extracted' in the dashboard.

findings.detail: 'Anthropic' is catalogued as a tool with a template description. Anthropic is the company, not a product. Still unfixed after 2 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'anthropic' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into the 'claude' tool entry. Already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef.

findings.detail: 'Openai' (incorrect casing, should be 'OpenAI') is catalogued as a tool. OpenAI is the company; ChatGPT, GPT-4, etc. are its products and already have separate entries. Still unfixed after 2 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'openai'/'Openai' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into 'chatgpt'. Already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef.

findings.where: data/tools.json — 33 of 312 entries (10.6%) have template descriptions
findings.detail: 33 tool entries use describe_tool() template patterns ('enhances productivity through AI-powered features', 'automates workflows', etc.). Proportional share improved (10.6% vs 31.4% last review) because the library grew 2.5×, but the root cause — describe_tool() in analyze_batch.py — is still unfixed and will re-infect the catalog on every analyze_batch.py run.
findings.suggestion: Fix describe_tool() in src/analyze_batch.py to extract real content from transcripts. The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module should back-fill existing template descriptions where transcripts are available.

findings.detail: analyze_batch.py still generates skill records with three hollow template fields: use_case ('Using {tool} for {category} tasks.'), output ('{tool} produces {category}-focused outputs.'), and relevance ('{tool} is featured as an AI tool in this video.'). skills.json currently has 0% boilerplate fields because the CLAUDE.md path generates real content — but if analyze_batch.py runs on raw text it will re-introduce templates.
findings.suggestion: Extract use_case and relevance from the transcript. If no qualifying sentence is found, use null/empty rather than a template string.

findings.where: data/daily_news.json (59/59 empty) + data/weekly_news.json (150/204 empty) + data/monthly_news.json (399/584 empty)
findings.detail: WORSENED: 608 of 847 video news entries (72%) now have empty summaries — up from 273/693 (39%) last review. Daily is now 100% empty (all 59 entries). Weekly jumped from 53% to 73%. The root cause is 100% transcript fallback rate (76/76 new videos). fill_missing_summaries is not clearing the backlog.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module must generate 1-sentence summaries from available description text for no-transcript videos — even 'Video about {tools_found}: {title}' is better than blank. Also address the transcript-failure root cause (finding 8a1b5c4d6e).

findings.detail: MCP connector detection uses a hardcoded list of only 8 specific string patterns (filesystem, browser, github, postgres, sqlite, memory, slack, google drive). Any other MCP server mentioned in a video is silently ignored. CLAUDE.md Step 8 specifies exhaustive MCP hunting — this code path misses the vast majority. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Broaden detection: capture any pattern matching 'npx .+-mcp', 'uvx .+-mcp', 'mcpServers', 'smithery', or 'mcp.so' in the text as a generic MCP connector, extracting the name from the matched string.

findings.detail: Slash-command regex r'/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,20}\b' matches URL path segments (/api, /v1), prose slashes, and file paths. The exclusion list only blocks 14 single-character tokens. Current commands.json shows only real commands because the CLAUDE.md path generates them correctly — but if analyze_batch.py runs on raw text it will accumulate false positives. Code bug still present.
findings.suggestion: Add a context requirement: only record a slash command if it appears adjacent to known AI tool names or a command-demonstration phrase. Extend blocklist to path prefixes (/api, /v1, /v2, /src, /static, /docs).

findings.detail: The tool is stored as 'Chatgpt' (wrong casing) instead of the correct brand name 'ChatGPT'. This is among the most-mentioned tools (114 mentions) and the casing error appears for every visitor. Already queued as suggestion 253d755074. Still unfixed after 2 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Rename name to 'ChatGPT' in data/tools.json. Suggestion 253d755074 is already queued — approve it.

findings.detail: fetch_playlist_videos calls request.execute() with no retry or error handling for YouTube API quota exhaustion (HttpError 429/503). If the quota is hit mid-pagination (playlist has 1333+ items across ~27 pages), the function raises an unhandled exception and the entire fetch run fails. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap request.execute() in a retry loop with exponential backoff for 429/503, up to 3 attempts, before re-raising.

findings.detail: write_skill_md() in analyze_batch.py (L402) opens SKILL.md output files with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. Additionally, main() opens pending JSON files (L725-726, L747-748) without encoding. Hebrew content or Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 runners. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to all remaining open() calls: analyze_batch.py lines 402, 725-726, 747-748.

findings.detail: In git_commit_push(), the retry loop calls git pull without checking its return code. If pull fails (merge conflict, auth failure), code continues and retries push on a broken state, exhausting all 3 retries without diagnosis. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Check the return code of git pull: if pr2.returncode != 0, log stderr and return early.

findings.detail: Tab buttons show no item count. Competitors (Future Tools, TAAFT) display per-category counts. The dashboard shows 209 skills and 312 tools but the nav buttons say nothing. The header 'Total skills' counter shows 171 (status.json value) rather than actual 209. Still unfixed after 2 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: After loading each tab's data in the init() async block, inject item counts into nav buttons from loaded JSON arrays (not status.json). ~10 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 3693c44f40.

findings.detail: Skills and Tools tabs have no sort control. Users can only filter by category; they cannot sort by newest, mentions, or reverse quality. All four benchmark competitors offer multi-axis sort. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add a sort <select> or pill-toggle above each card list: Quality (default) | Mentions | Newest. Client-side sort on the already-loaded array. ~20 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 72e04d9c61.

findings.detail: No hero tagline explains what Excavatortron is. First-time visitors see 'Excavatortron — AI Skills Tracker' and a search box with no context. All four competitors have a 2-3 sentence value proposition above the fold. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence beneath the subtitle: 'Tracks AI techniques, tools, models, and MCP connectors extracted from a curated YouTube playlist — updated automatically, quality-scored, and searchable.'

findings.detail: Inline Python in both workflows uses datetime.datetime.utcnow() which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and will emit DeprecationWarning. When GitHub Actions upgrades to Python 3.13+, this may become a hard error. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' with datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() in both workflow inline scripts.

findings.detail: renderAlert builds el.innerHTML = msg where msg contains raw HTML tags hardcoded in JS alongside esc(status.token_hint). The esc() call protects the dynamic value but the pattern (mixing safe-markup with partially-escaped content) is fragile — a future maintainer adding another dynamic field may forget esc(). Data comes from repo-committed JSON (low external risk) but the pattern is worth fixing. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Build the alert using DOM methods (createElement, textContent) rather than innerHTML, or create a dedicated safe-template function that always escapes dynamic values.

findings.detail: main() always sorts pending records newest-first (reverse=True at line 728), regardless of the workflow's order instruction. The analyze.yml workflow outputs 'order=oldest_first' for normal runs but analyze_batch.py ignores this entirely — has no --order parameter. CLAUDE.md Step 1 specifies oldest_first as the normal default. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add an --order argument to analyze_batch.py (default 'oldest_first'). Sort ascending when oldest_first. Pass the workflow plan step's order value to the script via argument or env var.

findings.detail: /tmp/sorted_pending.json is written on first call and reused on subsequent calls within the same runner. GitHub Actions may reuse warm runners for back-to-back analyze jobs. If the file exists from a previous run, newly added pending videos are absent. The file is never deleted on startup. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Delete /tmp/sorted_pending.json at the start of every main() invocation before checking if it exists, or unconditionally regenerate it on each call.

findings.detail: WORSENED: Three dashboard counters are now stale: total_skills=171 vs actual 209 (−38, 18% undercount); total_tools=290 vs actual 312 (−22); total_connectors=41 vs actual 48 (−7). Root cause: fetch.py overwrites these counters at fetch-stage runtime before analyze runs, so every fetch resets them to pre-analyze values. The dashboard header and counters show wrong numbers to every visitor.
findings.suggestion: Two-part fix: (1) Remove total_skills, total_tools, total_connectors from fetch.py's status.update() block. (2) In the analyze stage, after saving each data file, update the corresponding status counter: len(skills_data['skills']), len(tools_data['tools']), len(conns_data['connectors']).

findings.detail: DUAL PROBLEM: (1) 51 phantom slugs in index.json have no matching skill in skills.json — these block those slugs from being re-added (phantom count stable at 51, no longer growing). (2) 94 valid skills in skills.json are NOT indexed — analyze_batch.py would treat these as new on next run and append duplicates. Total coverage: index covers only 115/209 skills (55%). The reconciliation suggestion (a1b3c5d7e9) only fixes problem 1; problem 2 is new.
findings.suggestion: On main() startup: (1) remove phantom keys (not in skills slugs); (2) ADD missing valid skills to index. Loop through skills_data['skills'] and if slug not in index_data, add it: index_data[s['slug']] = {'score': s.get('quality_score',0), 'video_quality_score': s.get('video_quality_score'), 'starred': s.get('starred',False), 'target_tool': s.get('target_tool','claude')}. Then re-save.

findings.detail: create_news_summary() generates generic fallback text for videos with no real description: '{title}. AI content video featuring tools and techniques.' With 100% transcript fallback rate (76/76 new videos), every news summary written this run is generic filler. This is the direct engine cause of the 608 empty/low-quality news summaries (72% of total).
findings.suggestion: For no-transcript videos, generate a 1-sentence summary from the video title and any available tags/description text. Even 'Video about {tools_found}: {title}' is more useful than the generic template. Also add a 'summary_quality' field ('full'/'description'/'title_only') so the news tab can badge thin summaries.

findings.detail: fetch.py resets status['total_skills'] (and total_tools, total_connectors) to pre-analyze counts on every run. Since fetch runs first and analyze runs after, these counters are always one full fetch cycle stale. This is the root cause of the triple counter mismatch in status.json (see c9f2d8b4a1).
findings.suggestion: Remove total_skills, total_tools, total_connectors from the status.update() block in fetch.py. Let the analyze stage own these counters exclusively.

findings.detail: cu_state = json.load(open(cu_path, encoding='utf-8')) opens the file without a context manager (no with statement), so the file descriptor is never explicitly closed. In CPython this is collected promptly but is not safe in PyPy or other runtimes, and static analysis tools flag it. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in a with statement: with open(cu_path, encoding='utf-8') as fh: cu_state = json.load(fh).

findings.detail: key = f"{display_name}|" is assigned and never read. This dead-code line was presumably introduced when models were keyed by name|version, but the lookup now uses name-only comparison. Harmless but misleading. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Delete line 550 (key = f"{display_name}|"). No other change needed.

findings.detail: Quick-read mode hides ALL .card .sub elements globally. On the Connectors tab this removes the provider/category/source line ('Anthropic · integration · src: Community') which is essential for evaluating a connector. On the News tab it removes the source name and publication date. REVIEW.md requires Quick-read to condense uniformly across every tab; this degrades Connectors and News more than Skills. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace the global rule with targeted selectors: only apply .sub display:none to skill and tool cards. Add explicit exceptions for .newscard .sub and .connectors-card .sub, or add a .no-qr-hide class to sub elements that should always show.

findings.detail: NEW FINDING: The daily news feed is now 100% empty summaries (59/59). Every new video in this fetch run (76/76 no transcript) produced a blank news entry. The daily feed is the most prominent tab for returning visitors. Showing '(summary pending)' on every daily item makes the feed completely useless for its core purpose.
findings.suggestion: Treat this as emergency: the improve stage must fill_missing_summaries from description text with priority on daily entries. Even a 1-sentence title-derived summary is better than blank. Consider a daily cron that specifically back-fills the most recent 10 daily news entries from description.

findings.where: data/index.json — 94 valid skills in skills.json have no index entry
findings.detail: NEW FINDING: index.json covers only 115 of 209 valid skills (55%). The 94 unindexed skills represent mostly recently-added skills from the CLAUDE.md path. If analyze_batch.py processes a new video whose skill slug matches one of these 94, it will see the slug as 'absent' in index and APPEND A DUPLICATE record to skills.json. This is a data-corruption risk that grows as more skills are added without being indexed.
findings.suggestion: On main() startup, after dropping phantom index keys, also ADD all missing valid slugs to the index. One pass through skills_data['skills']: for each skill not in index_data, add it with its current score/quality/target_tool fields. This also fixes problem 1 (phantoms) and problem 2 (missing) in one reconciliation pass.

findings.detail: NEW FINDING: All skill and tool cards use identical visual styling regardless of quality rank, category, or score. A quality-9 skill looks the same as a quality-3 skill. Competitors (Future Tools, Product Hunt AI) use tool logos, gradient category headers, and tiered visual hierarchy. The dashboard reads as a flat undifferentiated list — the primary complaint from anyone comparing it to a polished competitor. This is identified in config.json as a top-3 priority (professional_design.target_rank: 'top_3') but no concrete visual change has been applied.
findings.suggestion: One concrete, significant step this cycle: add a colored left-border to skill/tool cards by score band — 3px solid green for score ≥8, amber for 6–7, grey for <6. This costs one CSS rule per band and zero JS. It instantly gives the card list a quality-ladder look without requiring images or external resources.

top_actions: CRITICAL — Fix the news summary crisis (daily 100% empty, 72% total): implement fill_missing_summaries in the improve stage to generate 1-sentence summaries from description text for no-transcript videos. Also fix the hardcoded TODAY in analyze_batch.py:20 (now 10 days stale) so recency penalties are correct and the rating system isn't systematically off.

Fix the triple status.json counter mismatch (skills 171 vs 209, tools 290 vs 312, connectors 41 vs 48) in two steps: (1) remove total_skills/total_tools/total_connectors from fetch.py status.update() so fetch stops overwriting them; (2) update all three counters in the analyze stage after each append. The dashboard currently shows wrong numbers to every visitor.

Fix the index.json dual problem (51 phantoms blocking new skills + 94 valid skills not indexed = only 55% coverage): on main() startup, reconcile by dropping phantom keys AND adding all unindexed valid skills in one pass. Without this, analyze_batch.py will create duplicate skill records for 94 slugs next time it runs.

Add encoding='utf-8' to ALL remaining bare open() calls in analyze_batch.py (L153, 161, 402, 725-726, 747-748) and process_video.py — high-severity data corruption on non-UTF-8 runners with Hebrew transcripts or Unicode tool names.

Quick wins (each ≤20 lines): (1) fix ChatGPT casing and remove Anthropic/Openai company-as-tool entries (suggestions already queued — approve them); (2) add color-coded left-border to skill/tool cards by score band (green ≥8, amber 6–7, grey <6) as the professional_design step this cycle; (3) add item counts to nav tabs from loaded JSON arrays; (4) add one-sentence hero tagline under the H1 subtitle.
